sources.title: Fiat-Shamir Transformation
sources.role: current implementation guidance for session identifiers, codecs, instance binding, serialization, parsing, and negative tests
sources.boundary: work in progress, not a final RFC or a substitute for protocol-specific theorem applicability

sources.title: Interactive Oracle Proofs
sources.authors: Eli Ben-Sasson, Alessandro Chiesa, and Nicholas Spooner
sources.role: IOP model, BCS compiler, Merkle/oracle compilation, and state-restoration characterization
sources.boundary: the compiler theorem requires exact source properties and random-oracle assumptions; it is not verifier implementation verification

sources.title: How not to Prove Yourself: Pitfalls of the Fiat-Shamir Heuristic and Applications to Helios
sources.authors: David Bernhard, Olivier Pereira, and Bogdan Warinschi
sources.role: strong-versus-weak FS and adaptive Statement binding
sources.boundary: three-move/adaptive theorem scope must not be generalized without a separate result

sources.title: Weak Fiat-Shamir Attacks on Modern Proof Systems
sources.authors: Quang Dao, Jim Miller, Opal Wright, and Paul Grubbs
sources.role: modern weak-FS survey and attacks across deployed proof-system families
sources.boundary: case-study prevalence is not a theorem about every protocol or implementation

sources.title: Fiat-Shamir in the Wild
sources.authors: Hieu Nguyen, Uyen Ho, and Alex Biryukov
sources.role: implementation-error taxonomy: Statement omission, ambiguous encoding, missing messages, brute force, and multi-round issues
sources.boundary: taxonomy and examples do not supply a security proof for zkc

sources.title: The Last Challenge Attack on Fiat-Shamir in KZG-based SNARKs
sources.authors: Oana Ciobotaru, Maxim Peter, and Vesselin Velichkov
sources.role: concrete final-challenge dependency and proof-forgery case
sources.boundary: KZG batching case does not imply a universal dependency rule beyond its selected protocol semantics

sources.title: How to Prove False Statements: Practical Attacks on Fiat-Shamir
sources.authors: Dmitry Khovratovich, Ron D. Rothblum, and Lev Soukhanov
sources.role: natural-protocol pressure on concrete random-oracle instantiation and circuit-dependent security
sources.boundary: an attack family against selected GKR-derived constructions is not a universal concrete-hash impossibility

sources.title: Fiat-Shamir Transformation of Multi-Round Interactive Proofs
sources.authors: Thomas Attema, Serge Fehr, and Michael Klooss
sources.role: multi-round special-soundness transport and quantitative security loss
sources.boundary: the current zkc import is a selected classical adaptive family, not a generic FS theorem

sources.title: The Measure-and-Reprogram Technique 2.0: Multi-Round Fiat-Shamir and More
sources.authors: Jelle Don, Serge Fehr, and Christian Majenz
sources.role: multi-input QROM reprogramming, ordered extraction, and query-loss pressure
sources.boundary: QROM transport needs its own adversary model and theorem applicability; it is not inherited from classical ROM

sources.title: VCVio: A Formally Verified Forking Lemma and Fiat-Shamir Transform, via a Flexible and Expressive Oracle Representation
sources.role: evidence that computational FS reductions and oracle operations can be mechanized
sources.boundary: the formalization covers its selected sigma-protocol framework; it does not verify arbitrary zkc protocols, codecs, lowerings, or deployments

sources.title: A Fiat-Shamir Transformation From Duplex Sponges
sources.role: ideal-permutation duplex construction, codec bias, salt, state-restoration, and indifferentiability limitations
sources.boundary: zkc's recorded proof-level source-validation findings block theorem activation pending repair or independent validation

sources.title: On Soundness Notions for Interactive Oracle Proofs
sources.authors: Alexander R. Block, Albert Garreta, Pratyush Ranjan Tiwari, and Michal Zajac
sources.role: relationships among special, RBR, and RBR-knowledge soundness and selected QROM transport
sources.boundary: the implications are directional; one soundness notion must not be substituted for another

sources.title: Fiat-Shamir Security of FRI and Related SNARKs
sources.authors: Alexander R. Block, Albert Garreta, Jonathan Katz, Justin Thaler, Pratyush Ranjan Tiwari, and Michal Zajac
sources.role: FRI and related-SNARK RBR analysis and BCS compilation boundary
sources.boundary: protocol-specific RBR results and assumptions cannot be inferred from a FRI-shaped schedule

sources.title: Plonky3 MultiField32Challenger: transcript malleability and challenge entropy loss
sources.role: distinct transcript aliases from missing length separation, radix mismatch, modular collapse, and high-bit truncation
sources.boundary: the package's finite aliases are class witnesses, not an exploit reproduction or audit of patched releases

sources.title: Purported opened values not included in transcript
sources.role: missing prover-controlled values before later challenges
sources.boundary: incident evidence is implementation-specific and does not itself prove the repaired protocol

sources.title: PaddingFreeSponge is not collision resistant for inputs of different lengths
sources.role: variable-length sponge-state aliases and the fixed-length-use boundary
sources.boundary: the advisory explicitly narrows impact when input length is fixed in advance

sources.title: Post Mortem: ZK ElGamal Proof Program Bug
sources.role: omitted algebraic proof components enabled arbitrary accepted proofs
sources.boundary: the report states no known exploitation and is not a general proof-system analysis

sources.title: The Frozen Heart Vulnerability in PlonK
sources.role: public-input omission and weak-FS incident family
sources.boundary: disclosure analysis supports the attack class, not a theorem or current implementation status
